correctness.rationale: For n >= 4 under independent atomless margins the rank vector is uniform. Equation (2.4) of arxiv:2108.06828 reduces exactly to S(pi)=the two path-power edge weights min(pi_i,pi_j) plus pi_{n-1}+2pi_n. The three orthogonal permutation modules of edge arrays (constants, centered vertex sums, and zero-vertex sums) are irreducible because the edge-pair commutant has dimension three. Real matrix-coefficient orthogonality gives direct and inverse random quadratic-assignment moments. Explicit edge and vertex sums yield E S=(n+1)(4n+3)/6, Var S=(n+1)(4n^2+14n+35)/180, Cov(S,S_inverse)=(4n^4+n^3+11n^2-127n+147)/(18n(n-1)). The ratio, positive decomposition, and the n=5 unique maximum follow from exact rational algebra; the difference polynomial has a positive-coefficient expansion at n=5. The embedded standard-library checker executed 5915 exact assertions: brute-force all permutations n=4..8, independent projection construction n=4..40, and rational inequalities to n=500. Enumeration supports but does not replace the all-n analytical derivation. No bivariate limit law is asserted.

originality.rationale: The nearest full-text papers introduce M-neighbor xi and calculate its marginal behavior (arxiv:2108.06828), or determine the reverse-direction joint law only for the original Chatterjee statistic and explicitly defer M>=2 (arxiv:2205.01769, Sec. 4). A later Chatterjee-Spearman paper (arxiv:2406.16859, Sections 2.1-2.2) still treats the original one-neighbor xi. Thus the inspected statements do not imply the M=2 reverse-direction exact covariance/correlation, unique n=5 maximum, or 10/n leading correlation. A previous lower-range bound for exactly the same M=2 score does not imply joint moments. Searches of published mathematical findings, exact phrases, and inverse-permutation aliases surfaced only related but nonimplicative records. Classical Johnson-decomposition theory and marginal moments are not represented as new; historical literature may contain an implicit equivalent and remains a documented risk.

value.rationale: The inspected symmetrization study arxiv:2205.01769 explicitly raises joint analysis for multi-neighbor Lin-Han coefficients; two right neighbors are its first genuinely extended case. The exact finite-n covariance and 10/n correlation decay control the degree to which two seemingly distinct directional rank statistics carry redundant information under an independence null. The sharp n=5 correlation peak makes the finite-sample dependence quantitatively important; computing inverse covariance cannot be inferred from the mean or marginal variance. The theorem is an intrinsically motivated exact joint-moment answer, not merely a routine tabulation. It does not purport to settle the more ambitious joint-CLT and test-calibration problems.
